name: strings
porting_notes: Custom standalone implementation (not a GNU binutils port). Scans files byte-by-byte using fread() in buffered 4096-byte blocks (perf-optimizer applied: 3-5x speedup over fgetc on 68000). Supports -a (whole-file scan), -n (minimum length), and -t (offset format d/o/x). Offset printing uses %7ld/%7lo/%7lx with AmigaOS-correct LONG format. Memory-checker audit: CLEAN (no leaks on any exit path, single static buffer, no dynamic allocation). 38/38 FS-UAE tests pass covering all flags, edge cases, error paths, and real-world binary scanning.
known_limitations: The -a flag is accepted but is a no-op (full-file scan is already the default behavior, as the ELF text-section-only mode from GNU binutils is not applicable on AmigaOS). No wide-character support (ASCII printable only, as expected on AmigaOS).

strings - Find printable strings in files

Ported by Duncan Bowring using amiport (AI-assisted porting toolkit).
Project: https://github.com/bdgscotland/amiport

Cross-compiled with m68k-amigaos-gcc for AmigaOS 3.x (68000+).
Tested in FS-UAE with AmigaOS 3.1.

Usage:
  strings [-a] [-n number] [-t format] [file ...]

Options:
  -a          Scan entire file (default behavior)
  -n number   Minimum string length (default: 4)
  -t format   Print offset (d=decimal, o=octal, x=hex)

Includes full source code and PORT.md.
